To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the Edwardsiella T3SS is expressed under conditions that mimic the intracellular environment and is regulated through the EsrAB and EsrC regulatory systems.
the T3SS of E. ictaruri is expressed in a pH- and phosphate-dependent manner and is regulated by EsrAB and EsrC, and that the plasmid-borne effector eseH is upregulated by EsrC.
the E. icaluri T3SS is regulated by pH and phosphate concentration via the EsrAB regulatory system, and that the AraC-family protein EsrC regulates the T3SS and a putative T6SS.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular mechanism of Edwardsiella icaluri pathogenesis and the role that type III and type VI secretion systems play in this process.
the molecular regulation of a T3SS and a putative T6SS in the fish pathogen E. ictulri.
the regulation of the Edwardsielli ictaluri (E. ictalur) type III secretion system.

EsrB is a global transcriptional regulator that controls expression of a number of virulence factors in the T3SS and T6SS, whereas EsrC is a more specific regulator that induces expression of the T3SS chaperone/secreted effector and the putative T6SS translocon protein under conditions that mimic the intracellular environment.
EsrA and its cognate sensor kinase EsrB are required for E. ichtaluri virulence and that EsrC plays an additional role in virulence by inducing expression of eseH and evpC.
